title: Rezoning for affordable housing at 450-470 King Street East
subtitle: Parkland concerns, public engagement, parking, Rangers celebration, regional water capacity update and a closed session on negotiations and litigation.
overview: Council approved a zoning by-law amendment for 450-470 King Street East, a City-owned site planned for affordable housing run by Kitchener Housing Inc. {{vote:m1}}. Council also endorsed the Urban Design Report and directed staff to apply it through a future site plan approval process. The by-law was added to the agenda for third reading so it could take effect the same day.

The one delegate asked for a park on the site and for the funding agreements to be made public. Staff said the planning recommendation was made separately from the funding work, and that a parkland acquisition strategy will come forward this term, with other possible parkland sites in King East. Kitchener Housing Inc. said all units would meet the Build Canada Homes definition of affordability, with at least 25 per cent deeply affordable.

Council then agreed to meet in closed session on a negotiations matter and a potential litigation matter {{vote:m2}}. The minutes report no outcome from that session. The Mayor also noted that Region of Waterloo council will consider a risk-based approach to water capacity and development later in the week. Council marked Pride Month, Seniors Month and National Indigenous History Month, and congratulated the Kitchener Rangers on their Memorial Cup win.

decisions.detail: Council approved the City-initiated zoning by-law amendment for the site, in the form of the proposed by-law and map {{vote:m1}}.
Council endorsed the May 2026 Urban Design Report and directed staff to implement it through a future Site Plan Approval process.
Council authorized a closed meeting after the special meeting to consider a negotiations matter and a potential litigation matter.

debate: A delegate opposed the application, arguing the neighbourhood needs a park and that land not used for parkland now is unlikely to become parkland later. The delegate asked council to state that funding agreements and earlier public commitments did not bind its vote, to table the relevant funding conditions publicly, and to weigh the application against the official plan.

Staff replied that the planning recommendation was made by staff not involved in the funding application. They said one funding source requires the City to keep ownership for at least five years, which staff plan to meet through a land lease. They agreed King East needs parkland and pointed to a parkland acquisition strategy.

One councillor asked about parking. Staff said a comparable Kitchener Housing Inc. downtown building has few residents with vehicles. Tenants needing parking would be matched to units elsewhere, and the site would offer short-term visitor parking.

One councillor asked about engagement and about the difference between informing and consulting. Staff said the project was first announced as an as-of-right development needing no consultation, and consultation began once the application sought more height and density. They said it included a session at the market and a virtual neighbourhood meeting.

A councillor supported the application but said residents in King East feel underserved and mistrust the process. The councillor asked staff and council to take care to rebuild trust and to work with a new neighbourhood association.
